newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still up near new highs late.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still up near new highs late.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were still holding sharp gains late Wednesday, in a fairly active session that saw firm cash and strong technicals drive most of the board to new contract highs, sources said.

At 1400 EDT, June, which hit a new high of $2.42 at midday, was still up by 8.6 cents at $2.395 per million British thermal units. July remained 7.2 cents higher at $2.41 after earlier setting a new benchmark of $2.435.

"We broke over the ($2.385 June) contract high and hit a lot of stops. It looks like we could take a run at $2.44," said one Midwest trader, adding reports of some unexpected power unit outages also helped fuel the rally.
Traders agreed news of unexpected power unit outages at Entergy's 936 MW River Bend nuclear unit in Louisiana and at Arizona Public Service's 750 MW coal unit helped stir some bullish sentiment.

While some still expected a profit taking pullback before weekly AGA stock data later today, most agreed the technical trend was still higher despite lingering doubts about the fundamental backing for the rally.
"The locals and funds have been driving it up and making the money. The trade has been selling into it," said one Texas-based trader.
Weather forecasts this week remained mixed, with hot temperatures expected to persist in the West, while the East, Midwest and South should range from normal to below-normal.
A Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for a weekly AGA stock build averaged 40-50 bcf versus a gain of 53 bcf a year ago.
Technically, traders now pegged resistance in June in the $2.47-50 area. Support was seen first at $2.20, with major buying likely at $2.05 and then along the up trendline around $2.04.

In the cash, Gulf Coast swing prices firmed 10 cents Wednesday to about the $2.30 area. Midcon pipes were up a similar amount to the $2.10-15 range. New York city gate gas firmed more than five cents to about $2.60.
NYMEX said 42,992 contracts traded at 1345 EDT.
On the KCBT, June firmed nine cents to $2.22, while deferreds were steady to 7.5 cents higher. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.4 cent to 17.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
